questions.q: In one attention head, what determines the mixing weights and what gets mixed?
choices: Values determine the weights; queries get mixed
Queries and keys determine the weights; values get mixed
The largest key becomes the next token
questions.why: Scaled query-key scores are masked and normalized; those weights multiply value vectors.

questions.q: Why may row i attend to position i in this next-token predictor?
choices: The model is allowed to peek at its target
The mask only matters at inference
The current input is known; the target is the following token
questions.why: Causality forbids j > i. Keeping the diagonal allows the current known input and ensures a nonempty row.

questions.q: The score tensor has shape (batch, receiving positions, source positions). Which axis must softmax normalize?
questions.why: Every receiver allocates its own unit of weight among available source positions; examples must not mix.

questions.q: What motivates dividing query-key dot products by sqrt(d_k)?
choices: It controls score growth with width under the paper's variance assumptions, reducing premature softmax saturation
It makes the output vocabulary smaller
questions.why: For independent zero-mean unit-variance coordinates the dot product variance grows with d_k. The scale is separate from masking and vector normalization.

questions.q: Keep values [2,0], [0,4], [6,2] and the causal mask, but set all queries to zero. What are the final weight row and final output?
questions.answer: The final weights are [1/3, 1/3, 1/3]; the output prints [2.666667, 2.000000].
questions.why: Equal zero scores have equal exponentials, so the last receiver averages all three values. Earlier rows average only their allowed prefix.

questions.q: In the exact-ratio example, hold Q and K fixed and increase only V[0,0] by 7. What happens to the weights and the final output's first coordinate?
questions.answer: All weights stay identical; the final output's first coordinate increases by 1.000000.
questions.why: The final receiver's weight for source zero is 1/7, so the change is (1/7)*7. Values do not enter the score calculation.

questions.q: Why do attention rows summing to one not prove that a decoder is causal? Describe a stronger test and its negative control.
rubric: Unmasked softmax also has rows summing to one
Check forbidden future weights are zero
Change only future inputs and verify earlier outputs remain unchanged
Repeat without the mask and confirm that the same perturbation changes earlier outputs
Run deterministic/no-dropout comparisons so randomness does not mimic leakage

questions.q: Explain attention to a programmer who thinks softmax already predicts the next word. Distinguish its output from a complete language model.
rubric: Queries and keys determine a distribution over available input positions
That distribution mixes values into a feature vector, not a token ID
A later vocabulary projection and softmax create next-token probabilities
An untrained head or hand-chosen example does not demonstrate learned language behavior

recall.q: What are the operations in one causal attention head?
recall.a: Project X into Q, K, V; compute QK-transpose divided by sqrt(d_k); replace future scores with negative infinity; softmax across source positions; multiply by V.

recall.q: Why does setting a forbidden score to zero fail?
recall.a: exp(0) is one, so the forbidden source retains positive weight. Negative infinity before softmax gives zero weight.

recall.q: What changes if only V changes, with Q and K fixed?
recall.a: Weights stay the same, but the output can change. Attention weights alone do not describe the entire output computation.

recall.q: What is a direct test of causal information flow?
recall.a: Perturb future inputs only and require earlier outputs to remain unchanged. Use an unmasked negative control to verify the perturbation can reveal leakage.

recall.q: What does scaling by sqrt(d_k) accomplish, and what does it not do?
recall.a: It controls dot-product magnitude growth under the usual initialization assumptions. It is not cosine normalization, a causal mask, or a guarantee of a learned semantic match.
